note: The frontends that consume the design system, and the ones that should.
This is a local audit, not a gate: the frontends are private and are not
cloned in CI, so a report computed on a machine that has them cannot be
reproduced on one that does not. The reports under profiles/frontend-audit/
are therefore a snapshot, and the tool is run where the clones are.
The mechanical half of each entry is measured by tools/audit_frontends.py.
The qualitative half — licence, namespace, evidence, verdict — was read out
of each repository by hand and is kept here so that the matrix can be

frontends.name: gnu6.live
frontends.stack: React 19 + React Router 8, Vite 8, TypeScript 6, XState, Drizzle, Zod
frontends.evidence: 21 test files, 12 QA screenshots, a11y audit v0.2/v0.3, release dossier, full-site manifest with sha256
frontends.blocks: the eight declared spacing steps are referenced zero times; features.css carries ~250 hardcoded hexes

frontends.name: engineering-corpus
frontends.stack: static generator (markdown-it-py) + vanilla JS, no framework
frontends.palette: three of five; the other two are declared but never referenced
frontends.components: ~60 classes in one file, no library
frontends.evidence: 48 files under evidence/runs, artifact manifest with sha256, screenshot manifest, axe audits, scripts/qualify.py refuses a dirty tree and demands two byte-identical rebuilds
frontends.blocks: a second :root in site/style.css overrides the declared tokens; 35 hardcoded hexes bypass them

frontends.name: diagram.studio
frontends.stack: Next.js 16 + React 19 + Tailwind 4 + Radix, shipped as an Electron app
frontends.namespace: own (--gnu-*, plus a shadcn HSL set and a --neo-* family)
frontends.palette: four of five; blue absent, shell and orange declared but unused
frontends.components: 39 component files, no variant prop — differentiation is by state
frontends.evidence: 121 test files, verify script, pre-push hook; no CI, no screenshots, no manifest
frontends.blocks: the shadcn HSL set and the --neo-* family are a second palette; the third-party copyright is a consent question, not a technical one

frontends.name: gnu.in.work
frontends.stack: pnpm monorepo, React 19 + Vite 6 + Tailwind 4 + shadcn, Electron shell
frontends.palette: two of five; the Radix scales are a second palette
frontends.components: 6 in packages/ui, 44 shadcn in apps/app, 12 in src/react-app/design-system
frontends.evidence: 122 test files, an 18-step verification script, four debt baselines enforced by a linter; no QA file
frontends.blocks: the largest job: 1262 colours outside the contract, most of them Radix scale values; PORTAGE.md already records the portage and its colour-literal rule

frontends.name: gnu.in.docs
frontends.components: 8 Astro components; StatusCard carries three data-driven state axes
frontends.evidence: 18 unit test files, Playwright, axe, 36 visual baselines, an audit-handoff severity register, six regression gates, manifests and a registry schema
frontends.note: The repository keeps the earlier design corpus beside the live site. The audit measures what the site ships.
frontends.blocks: no licence file, so nothing may be taken from it; the vendored Montreal faces are unlicensed. Its evidence discipline is stronger than the design system's own and should flow the other way

frontends.name: gnu6-live
frontends.stack: React 19 + React Router 8 SSR, Vite 8, TypeScript 6, XState, Drizzle
frontends.namespace: the gnosix namespace (21 --gnosix-* vars in public/gnu6/gnu6.css, a vendored gnu6-design 1.1.1)
frontends.palette: all five, in the gnosix namespace
frontends.components: app/design-system/ (8 files), app/context-system/ (24 primitives, 16 molecules, 8 recipes, 6 boards), app/shell/, app/features/
frontends.evidence: 52 vitest files, 16 Playwright specs, a proof directory with bundles, checksums and a verdict, 56 QA screenshots
frontends.blocks: no licence; a parallel --ctx-* palette; a 4853-line stylesheet that root.tsx does not link and that only the tests read; the design-system folder is duplicated from gnu6.live

frontends.name: gnu6-docs-portal
frontends.stack: a static offline prototype: a Python stdlib generator, no framework, no bundler, no package.json
frontends.licence: none; the content bundle carries "MIT where first-party rights permit"
frontends.namespace: a vendored gnu6-design 1.1.1 with 21 --gnosix-* names, of which 15 the system does not publish
frontends.palette: all five, under the camelCase spelling the system does not publish
frontends.components: 38 base components and 99 selectors in the vendored sheet; only the header shell is rendered
frontends.evidence: ten assertions in a build test, a four-page browser check, three lock files — and build.py never verifies the design lock
frontends.verdict: absorb seventh, if it is absorbed at all
frontends.blocks: not production-qualified, and the gnu6-live specification marks it a migration donor with no new deployment; its content bundle is produced by engineering-corpus, so it is downstream of another audited repo. Space Grotesk is shipped and never applied, because the @font-face lives in a sheet the served chain does not link, and the motion sheets read sixteen variables that sheet alone defines

frontends.name: gnosis.OS
frontends.stack: native GPUI, a sixty-crate Rust workspace, D-Bus and Wayland layer-shell
frontends.licence: AGPL-3.0 at the root; 47 crate manifests say GPL-3.0-or-later — they disagree
frontends.palette: four of five at runtime; the blue is never used, the runtime blue is #3D8DCC
frontends.components: 12 widgets in engine/gnosis-ui/src/, 8 atoms and 7 molecules in the bar
frontends.evidence: 2291 Rust tests across 182 files, 85 shell contract tests, 58 screenshots, a surface screenshot manifest, components.toml and contracts/surfaces.toml
frontends.blocks: AGPL cannot flow into an MIT repository, so the flow is one way only; the token source engine/blob.in/tokens.json is already a codegen pipeline and should become a projection of core/TOKENS.json

frontends.name: blob.in-showcase
frontends.role: claims the design system without consuming it
frontends.stack: native Rust, winit + wgpu + egui, Wayland
frontends.licence: LicenseRef-Proprietary, no licence file, never publish
frontends.palette: none of the five; a cyan accent where the system has an orange one
frontends.components: a UI-tree core and a scene crate, a shell of egui panels
frontends.evidence: 30 evidence run directories, qualification and run records, 68 screenshots, 86 logs, 227 Rust tests
frontends.blocks: theme.rs:1 says the palette is read from a gnosix path that does not exist and does not match the current palette; the claim must be corrected before anything else

frontends.name: spjoaillerie-live
frontends.stack: a capture of a live storefront: React 18 UMD transpiled in the browser, no build, one commit
frontends.palette: none of the five; a gold and parchment brand
frontends.components: a sixteen-component compiled bundle with source hashes
frontends.evidence: none: no tests, no CI, no evidence directory, no manifest, no licence
frontends.blocks: it is a capture of a different brand. Absorbing it would import Didot, Garamond and gold into the system. One idea is worth taking — the bundle header that records where each component came from — and the brand is left alone
